definitions.explanation: Expresses strong certainty that something will happen.
Indicates that something happens every time without exception.

examples.japanese: {明日|あした}{必|かなら}ず{来|き}てください。
{必|かなら}ず{成功|せいこう}する。
{彼|かれ}は{必|かなら}ず{約束|やくそく}を{守|まも}る。
{出|で}かける{前|まえ}に{必|かなら}ず{戸締|とじ}まりをする。
examples.english: I always lock up before going out.

examples.japanese: {努力|どりょく}すれば{必|かなら}ず{報|むく}われる。
examples.english: If you make an effort, you will surely be rewarded.

examples.japanese: {必|かなら}ず{連絡|れんらく}してね。
examples.english: Make sure to contact me, okay?

examples.japanese: {朝|あさ}{必|かなら}ず{新聞|しんぶん}を{読|よ}む。
examples.english: I always read the newspaper in the morning.

examples.japanese: {必|かなら}ずしも{正|ただ}しいとは{限|かぎ}らない。
{食事|しょくじ}の{前|まえ}に{必|かなら}ず{手|て}を{洗|あら}う。
examples.english: I always wash my hands before meals.

notes:
{必|かなら}ず is an adverb expressing certainty or 'without exception.'

Position: Usually appears before the verb, often near the beginning of the clause.

Modifies: Verbs (both actions and states)

[Register: Neutral]

Similar adverbs:
- {必|かなら}ず vs. きっと: Both express certainty. {必|かなら}ず emphasizes 'without fail' (100% certainty); きっと expresses confident expectation (high probability but not absolute).
- {必|かなら}ず vs. {絶対|ぜったい}(に): {絶対|ぜったい}に is more emphatic and casual; {必|かなら}ず is more neutral.
- {必|かなら}ず vs. いつも: いつも simply means 'always'; {必|かなら}ず adds emphasis on 'without exception.'

Note: Often used in instructions, promises, and warnings to emphasize importance.
